### Findings

Returned item volume was queried for authorized products across all available historical records, filtering for items with status `'Returned'` grouped by catalogue brand [q1].

| brand | returned_items |
| :--- | :--- |
| South | 1 |

Both brands show an observed volume of 1 returned item each [q1]. Because each brand has only a single recorded return, this represents a very small sample size.

### Limitations

- **Scope & Population**: The analysis is restricted to items where `status = 'Returned'`. Total order item volume, completed sales, and return rates were not queried [q1].
- **Missing Dimensions**: Return reasons, customer keys, product-level identifiers, pricing, and temporal trends were not measured [q1].
- **Data Coverage**: The temporal boundaries and completeness of the historical dataset were not evaluated.

### Action items (proposed)

- **Return Rate Calculation**: Propose querying total item counts (or completed item counts) alongside returned items to calculate return rates by brand.
- **Product and Attribute Granularity**: Propose breaking down returned items by specific `product_id` and category within each brand to determine if returns are concentrated in specific models.
- **Temporal Analysis**: Propose querying item creation dates to assess whether return events occurred recently or over an extended duration.
